cases.note: The loop replicates the original if/else chain exactly: same thresholds in descending order (PB..KB) with 'B' as fallback and break on first match, so behaviour is unchanged.
The mutated explicit integer pattern '[-+]?0b' -> '[^-+]?0b' rejects signed binary literals like '!!int -0b1010', which previously loaded as -10 and now throws a resolve error.

cases.note: Equivalent refactor: the sign-stripping and prefix-slicing logic is unchanged, and the decimal branch already parsed the sign-stripped string, so parseInt(digits, 10) behaves identically.

The type check `type === 'string'` was removed, so non-string inputs with a truthy `.length` (including undefined, which now throws TypeError on property access, and objects/arrays) take the parse() path instead of throwing the documented invalid-input error.
